card: Stops monitoring socket exception sets in select() on non-Windows platforms, and disconnects established P2P peers on Windows if an exception triggers. On POSIX systems, TCP urgent data or out-of-band pointers can leave socket exceptions pending without readable data, causing network event loops to busy-spin. This serves as an alternative to PR 36688, avoiding SO_OOBINLINE per RFC 6093 recommendations.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the patch; previous description had no patch diff attached.
evidence: Commit 1fde57f1de states: 'Windows needs select's exception set to detect failed non-blocking connects. On other platforms, a TCP urgent pointer can leave the exception set pending even when no data is readable. Only monitor it on Windows, and disconnect established P2P peers if it is set.'
problem: Incoming TCP urgent data sets the socket exception condition in select(). On POSIX systems where urgent data is not read, this can leave the exception pending and cause the network event loop to spin in a busy loop. Bitcoin Core does not use out-of-band data, but Windows still requires monitoring the exception set to detect failed non-blocking connect calls.

risk.why: Altering select() socket event handling could inadvertently ignore connection failure errors on non-Windows platforms or disconnect valid peers on Windows.

summary: Restricts socket exception monitoring in select() to Windows, and disconnects established peers on Windows if an exception condition occurs. It also adds documentation explaining why Bitcoin Core's P2P layer does not enable SO_OOBINLINE.
